rationale: A further consequence of the configuration-recovery defect is cheap to test and materially different: the missing configuration is not only an in-memory view, because the node writes the committed configuration into the snapshot metadata it creates and restores that metadata at startup. This batch registers the additional sources and behaviour, plus one fixed experiment that shows the empty configuration reaching durable state and surviving a restart with the replay disabled.

knowledge.statement: takeSnapshot reads the configurations tracked by the main thread and passes the committed configuration and its committed index into SnapshotStore.Create, so the snapshot metadata is only as correct as the configuration state the node currently tracks; restoreSnapshot installs that same configuration and index into both committed and latest on startup, and the startup scan then starts above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied).
knowledge.conditions: Applies to user and automatic snapshots on any node state, and to every startup that restores a snapshot (snapshot.go:155-190, api.go:653-684).

scope.description: Three in-memory voters A, B and C. A command is committed, A is shut down and restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot on its stores, and the harness records A's tracked configuration and the newest configuration entry in A's log. A command is committed again so A's FSM has something to snapshot, A takes a snapshot through the normal path, and the harness compares the snapshot's recorded configuration and configuration index with the configuration entry in A's log. A is then shut down and restarted again with the replay disabled, and the harness records the configuration the node comes up with.
assumptions: A's stores hold no snapshot before the first restart, so the flag-on startup replays the committed log above index 0 and the scan is skipped.
The snapshot is taken through the library's normal snapshot path (user snapshot request handled by the snapshot goroutine), so nothing in the harness supplies the configuration it records.
The second restart uses the same stores with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs false and a fresh in-memory FSM, so the configuration can only come from the snapshot metadata and the log scan.
The flag-off restart is expected to run without a leader in the observation window because an empty configuration prevents the node from starting an election.
excluded: No multi-node partition and no commit-rule consequence in this case; the earlier multi-node experiment covers that.
No production snapshot store, no process-level restart, and no case in which a later configuration entry above the snapshot index repairs the tracked configuration.
The harness does not attempt to remove the corrupt snapshot, so recovery by deleting durable state is not measured.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds three assuranceMultiNode values (random in-memory transport addresses, inmemConfig with RestoreCommittedLogs true, NewInmemCommitTrackingStore, NewInmemStore and NewInmemSnapshotStore per node), wires the transports pairwise, calls BootstrapCluster with the same three-voter configuration on each node and NewRaft with a fresh MockFSM each. It waits for a real leader, and if A won, moves leadership to B with LeadershipTransferToServer so that A can be restarted without stopping the cluster's leader. One command is committed and the harness waits until A's FSM has applied a command entry. A is shut down and a new transport on A's address is connected to B and C; NewRaft is called on A's stores with RestoreCommittedLogs true and a fresh MockFSM, and the harness records the tracked configurations through r.configurationsCh plus A's staged commit index, last index and newest configuration entry. One more command is committed and awaited in A's FSM, then A.Snapshot() is called and the harness reads the newest SnapshotMeta from A's snapshot store, comparing its Configuration and ConfigurationIndex with the log's configuration entry. A is shut down again, a further transport is created on the same address and connected to B and C, and NewRaft is called with RestoreCommittedLogs false; the harness records the restored snapshot index, the tracked configuration, the leader observation over 1500ms and the final state.
experiment.responsibility: raft's snapshot writer is responsible for recording the committed configuration that the node's log establishes, and raft's startup recovery is responsible for establishing membership from durable state; a node that loses its configuration must not write that loss into the durable record other nodes and later restarts depend on.

comparisons.description: The configuration recorded in the snapshot metadata must be the configuration the node's own log establishes, not the empty configuration the recovery left behind.

A restart with the replay disabled must not come up without a membership configuration when its own snapshot and log establish one; a violating witness shows the loss is durable rather than confined to the replay path.
